text:
Clouds have hung around all day and it's a mild 54 this afternoon, so sunset at 5:47 will likely be more gray than golden, though skies should break up a bit as the night goes on. Tonight turns partly cloudy and cool, with a low around 42.

Thursday is the better day. Sunshine, a breezy south wind, and a high near 65, a good 10 degrees warmer than today. Forecasters have it anywhere from the low 60s to near 70, so I'd bet on mid 60s. The wind gusts up near 30 mph in the afternoon, and with so many dry leaves on the ground, that makes it a day to be careful with any outdoor burning.

A cold front arrives Thursday evening. The forecast has a slight chance of a brief shower between 8 and 10, and the European model is wetter than the rest, but nothing that amounts to a real rain. Friday cools back down. I'd enjoy the afternoon outside Thursday and keep a light jacket handy for the evening.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: While conditions are not expected to reach Red Flag Criteria in the upcoming future, gusty conditions and lower relative humidity values will cause increased fire weather concerns due to plentiful dry leaves on the ground serving as fuel. Winds gusts tomorrow and Friday are generally expected to be in the 15 to 25 mph range, with some gusts up to 30 mph possible. The highest gusts are expected in the St. Lawrence Valley and northern slopes of the Adirondacks where gusts up to 35 mph are possible tomorrow. Relative humidity values will generally be in the 40-55 percent range tomorrow. Relative humidity values are expected in that range again on Friday for most places, but localized drops into the 30-40 percent range are possible in the Lower Connecticut River Valley. Heading into the weekend, winds will mostly remain under 15 mph. However, relative humidity values should drop into the 30-45 percent range for most places, with a localized drop into upper 20s possible in the Lower Connecticut Valley. A few showers are possible tomorrow evening and overnight, but a wetting rain is not expected anywhere. KEY MESSAGE 2: After a warm day tomorrow, a cold front comes through tomorrow night and into early Friday. A few showers are possible across northern New York and the higher elevations of northern Vermont but with dry air aloft and weak forcing, they will be brief and only lead to a couple hundreths of an inch of rain locally. The highest amounts are expected in the northern Greens and the Adirondacks. Strong cold air advection will occur on Friday with clouds in the typical upslope areas. Surface high pressure builds overhead into the weekend, leading to mostly sunny skies and moderating temperatures. The Halloween forecast looks great with clear skies, light winds and temperatures quickly dropping from the 50s into the 30s during the evening. However, despite clear skies, any added ambiance from the moon will mostly be missing as it was full a couple days ago and will rise around 10:45 Halloween evening. KEY MESSAGE 3: While no hazardous weather is expected, there is some disagreement amongst ensemble guidance on the upper level pattern early next week. The consensus idea amongst non-GEFS guidance strongly favors a more amplified ridge to our west maintaining northwest flow over our region and deflecting most precipitation well to our west. In this most likely scenario, low level temperatures remain above normal with near surface winds primarily out of the south and chances of rain are very low. While certainly not indicating any significant weather, the majority of GEFS membership in contrast suggests some weak troughing that allows a shortwave to push showers in from the west. As such, this less likely scenario brings rainfall chances closer to 60% to 75% in the Monday afternoon through Tuesday timeframe, and for amounts exceeding 0.25" mainly 20-30%, or slightly higher in the Adirondacks. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - While clouds and glum skies returned today, by tomorrow our stretch of sunny autumn days will restart tomorrow continues across Vermont and the North Country, with one more warm day ahead before a cold front sweeps through. Expect a mild and breezy Thursday with highs in the 60s, followed by gusty winds and just a few brief mountain showers Thursday night into Friday. Beyond that, high pressure takes control for a gorgeous Halloween weekend with plenty of sunshine and crisp fall temperatures. High pressure builds overhead for the weekend, bringing mostly sunny skies Saturday with highs near 51 and clear and chilly Saturday night near 35. Sunday stays sunny with highs near 55 ahead of a perfect Halloween evening, with clear skies, light winds and temperatures falling quickly from the 50s into the 30s for trick-or-treaters. The moon offers little extra light, rising around 10:45 at night. Seasonable and mainly dry weather continues into next week with highs in the mid to upper 50s Monday through Wednesday and only a very low chance for a shower early next week.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-27T22:07:00Z — same caveat): Mostly cloudy, but turning a bit milder Wednesday — Wednesday will feature a mostly cloudy sky, with a few more breaks of sun likely by afternoon. It turns a bit milder — highs rebound to the low and mid-50s. Thursday turns warmer, as a gusty south breeze sends highs to around 70. Expect lots of sunshine through the morning and afternoon. A cold front brings a band of clouds and spotty showers during the evening, lasting into the overnight. Friday turns mostly dry, with only a spot shower leftover. However, expect more clouds than sun with highs falling back to the 50s. Halloween weekend starts bright but cool on Saturday, with highs in the upper 40s. Sunday turns a bit milder, with highs in the mid-50s, as sun mixes with clouds. Most of next week looks mild for early November, with highs pushing past 60 several days in a row. Monday looks brightest, then more clouds and a greater chance for showers arrive by mid to late week.
